What programmes does Thames Wellness Academy offer? We offer Yoga Alliance Professionals certified Foundation Training, continuing professional development (CPD), specialist workshops, retreats and research collaborations. All programmes are teacher-led and delivered on site.

Are your courses certified? Yes. Thames Wellness Academy is certified by Yoga Alliance Professionals. Our Foundation Training pathways meet recognised standards for professional yoga and wellness teaching.

Where are programmes delivered? Our programmes are delivered on site across Berkshire, including dedicated training venues and partner studio locations. Specific venue details are shared when you enquire or apply.

How do I apply for Foundation Training? Visit our Join page to submit an application or enquiry. Tell us about your experience and goals, and our team will guide you through the next steps, including course dates and entry requirements.

Do you offer CPD for qualified teachers? Yes. Our CPD programmes support qualified teachers and wellness professionals who wish to deepen their practice in anatomy, breath work, therapeutic teaching and evidence-informed approaches.

Can organisations book workshops or training? We work with studios, corporate wellbeing teams and healthcare settings to deliver bespoke workshops and training. Contact us with your requirements and we will discuss tailored options.

journal/breath-work-in-teaching.html.title: Breath work in professional teaching practice | Thames Wellness Academy Journal
journal/breath-work-in-teaching.html.description: How diaphragmatic breath work supports stress regulation and safe, inclusive class delivery for wellness educators in Berkshire.
journal/breath-work-in-teaching.html.h1: Breath work in professional teaching practice
h2s: Why breath work matters in wellness education
paragraphs: How diaphragmatic breath work supports stress regulation, nervous system awareness and safe, inclusive class delivery for wellness educators across Berkshire.

For educators working in studios, schools, corporate settings and clinical environments across Berkshire, conscious breathing provides a bridge between movement, stillness and emotional regulation. When taught with care, it helps participants feel seen rather than instructed.

Diaphragmatic breathing encourages slower, deeper respiration that can support parasympathetic activation. In our on-site workshops, we observe how simple pacing cues help participants settle before more demanding movement sequences.
Trainees learn to notice their own breath patterns first. This self-awareness becomes the foundation for guiding others without imposing pace or intensity that may feel overwhelming.

A well-paced session often opens with grounding breath, transitions through movement with rhythmic cues, and closes with restorative breathing or guided stillness. This arc mirrors the nervous system journey many participants experience during a class.
We encourage educators to script fewer cues and listen more. Breath work is not a performance. It is a conversation between the teacher, the participant and the environment they share.
Conscious breath does not fix stress. It offers a pause wide enough for people to choose how they respond.

Focused breathing can be activating for some participants, particularly those with anxiety, respiratory conditions or trauma histories. Our programmes emphasise choice, agency and clear language that avoids commanding participants to breathe in a prescribed way.

Corporate wellness sessions, school outreach and studio classes often bring together people with widely varying experience. Layered instruction allows beginners and advanced practitioners to work at their own level within the same room.

We continue to refine our breath work modules through research collaboration, trainee feedback and supervision. Our goal is confident, compassionate educators who can adapt breath practices for real-world settings without losing rigour or safety.
Foundation Training Lead · Yoga Alliance Professionals

Leads 200-hour and advanced certification pathways at Thames Wellness Academy, with a focus on therapeutic teaching, supervised practicum and evidence-informed breath work across Berkshire programmes.
list_items: Observe without correcting: allow participants to find their own rhythm before offering refinement.
Pair breath with accessible movement so the practice feels embodied rather than abstract.
Offer seated, standing and supine variations to suit diverse bodies and energy levels.
Check in verbally and non-verbally so participants can opt out without pressure.
Always offer alternatives such as orienting to the room or gentle movement.
Avoid prolonged breath holds without explicit consent and medical awareness.
Never position breath work as a cure for mental health conditions.
Refer to clinical colleagues when participants need support beyond your scope.

journal/workshops-specialist-client-need.description: Supporting menopause, sleep health and musculoskeletal wellbeing through focused workshop training at Thames Wellness Academy in Berkshire.
h2s: Why specialist workshops matter for educators
paragraphs: Supporting menopause, sleep health and musculoskeletal wellbeing through focused, teacher-led workshop training delivered on-site across Berkshire.
Each workshop is teacher-led, delivered on-site across Berkshire venues, and aligned with Yoga Alliance Professionals continuing education standards.

Menopause affects energy, sleep, joint comfort and confidence. Workshops focus on temperature regulation strategies, strength maintenance and language that normalises experience without medicalising every symptom.

Poor sleep affects concentration, mood and recovery from physical activity. Educators learn to structure evening sessions that support relaxation without overstimulating the nervous system before rest.
Specialist workshops are not about becoming a clinician. They are about teaching with greater awareness and appropriate humility.
Many participants live with persistent discomfort. Workshops cover load management, joint-friendly modifications and communication that validates experience without promising cures.

Our cohorts include studio teachers, school staff, occupational health practitioners and therapists. Facilitators model how to layer content so everyone can apply learning within their own scope of practice.

We are developing further modules on workplace stress recovery, peri-menopause support and collaborative care with local clinical partners. Details will be published on our workshops page and shared through the journal.

journal/evidence-informed-wellness-educa.title: Evidence-informed wellness education | Thames Wellness Academy Journal
journal/evidence-informed-wellness-educa.description: Why research collaboration matters for credible teacher training and CPD programmes at Thames Wellness Academy in Berkshire.
paragraphs: Why research collaboration matters for credible teacher training, supervised practicum and continuing professional development across Berkshire.
Research collaboration is not about turning trainees into academics. It is about giving educators the confidence to explain why they teach what they teach, and when to adapt or refer.

Each Foundation Training and CPD module is reviewed against published literature, professional body guidance and feedback from supervised practicum. We distinguish clearly between established findings, emerging research and areas where honest uncertainty remains.
Educators need language that is accurate and accessible. We train cohorts to read summaries critically, question sensational claims and communicate benefits without overstating results.
Evidence-informed teaching is not about certainty. It is about humility, curiosity and clear boundaries.

Schools, corporate clients and clinical referrers increasingly ask for proof of programme quality. We share outcomes transparently, avoid cherry-picked statistics and never imply that wellness training replaces medical or psychological care.

Some cohort members arrive with healthcare experience; others come from education or creative fields. Differentiated resources help everyone engage with research at a level that builds confidence rather than intimidation.

We are expanding partnerships across Berkshire and the wider South East, with priorities in breath work, pain-aware movement and workplace wellbeing. Findings will continue to feed directly into curriculum updates and journal publications.
